title: Prefix Sum of Twos for Split Index
approach_explanation: Since the array elements are only 1 and 2, the product of any subarray is simply $2^{	ext{count of 2s}}$. For the product of the prefix of length $k$ to equal the product of the suffix from $k+1$ to $n$, the count of 2s in the prefix must equal the count of 2s in the suffix. We can precompute the total count of 2s or use a prefix sum array to keep track of the number of 2s up to each index. Then, we iterate through all possible split points $k$ from $1$ to $n-1$, check if the number of 2s in the left part equals the number of 2s in the right part, and return the first (smallest) $k$ that satisfies this condition.

code_breakdown.section_title: Test Case Loop and Input Reading
code_breakdown.explanation: Reads the number of test cases $t$, and for each test case, reads $n$ and initializes a prefix sum vector to store the cumulative count of 2s.
Iterates through the input elements, checking if each number is 2. Updates the prefix sum array such that `prefix[i]` stores the total number of 2s from index $0$ to $i$.

Iterates $i$ from $0$ to $n-2$ (corresponding to split index $k = i+1$). Computes the number of 2s in the prefix $a[0 	o i]$ as `prefix[i]` and in the suffix $a[i+1 	o n-1]$ as `prefix[n-1] - prefix[i]`. If they are equal, sets `ans = i+1` and terminates early to ensure the smallest $k$ is chosen.
Prints the computed index `ans` (or $-1$ if no valid $k$ was found) for each test case.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each test case, we make a single pass to read input and compute prefix sums, taking $O(n)$ time. We make a second pass of length $n-1$ to find the split index, which also takes $O(n)$ time. Over $t$ test cases, the total time complexity is $O(	extsum n)$, which is bounded by $O(n 	imes t) 	ext{ or } O(	ext{max } 	ext{sum of } n) 	ext{ i.e., } O(N_{	ext{total}})$.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: We allocate a vector `prefix` of size $n$ to store the prefix sums of 2s for each test case, which requires $O(n)$ auxiliary space.

strengths: Clean separation of test cases and efficient logic using prefix sums.
Early exit ensures the smallest index $k$ is found immediately.
Linear time complexity is optimal for this problem.
edge_cases_handled: Arrays with no 2s (all 1s), correctly handled since count of 2s on both sides is 0.
Arrays with odd/even numbers of 2s, correctly returning -1 when impossible.

optimization_and_alternatives.tradeoffs: Instead of storing prefix sums in a vector, we can count the total number of 2s in a first pass, and then iterate through the array a second time maintaining a running count of 2s, achieving $O(1)$ auxiliary space.
